Rapacity
/ruh-PAS-ih-tee/
noun
From Latin rapacitas, from rapax and rapio, to seize. Webster 1828 gives addictedness to plunder, the practice of seizing by force, and extorting by oppressive injustice.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Rapacity is the habit of seizing what belongs to another. They covet fields and take them by violence, and houses, and oppress a man and his heritage (Mic 2:2). The ways of everyone greedy of gain take away the life of the owners thereof (Prov 1:19). Woe to him that coveteth an evil covetousness to his house, that he may set his nest on high (Hab 2:9). The sin is not enterprise. It is plunder dressed as gain, and oppression dressed as success.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines RAPAC'ITY as addictedness to plunder; the act or practice of seizing by force; and the act or practice of extorting or exacting by oppressive injustice.

expand to see more

RAPAC'ITY, noun [Latin rapacitas, from rapax, rapio.]

1. Addictedness to plunder; the exercise of plunder; the act or practice of seizing by force; as the rapacity of a conquering army; the rapacity of pirates; the rapacity of a Turkish pashaw; the rapacity of extortioners.

2. Ravenousness; as the rapacity of animals.

3. The act or practice of extorting or exacting by oppressive injustice.

Key Scripture

Micah 2:2 — "And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage."

Proverbs 1:19 — "So are the ways of every one that is greedy of gain; which taketh away the life of the owners thereof."

Modern Corruption

Rapacity is rebranded as hustle, market discipline, or a winner's appetite, so long as the seizure is legal enough.

expand to see more

A conquering appetite for other men's fields does not become virtue because it files papers. Micah names the coveting and the violence together. Proverbs says the greedy way takes life, not merely margin.

Webster's third sense is exacting by oppressive injustice. Interest, rent, and office can all wear that face. The dictionary will not call plunder prudence.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin rapio is to seize. The KJV speaks of taking by violence, greed of gain, and evil covetousness. No Strong's number is invented for the English noun.

expand to see more

Latin rapacitas — addictedness to seizing by force.

KJV take them by violence joins coveting to oppression (Mic 2:2).

No invented Strong's tag for the English noun rapacity.

Usage

"Rapacity is the practice of seizing by force, not sharp business."

"Do not covet a man's field and call the taking success."

"Greed of gain takes away the life of its owners."
